detail.name: Roller XML-RPC
detail.verdictHint: Exploited, on CISA's list. No login. Fixed in 6.1.6.
detail.summary: A bug in Apache Roller, a Java blog server, lets anyone who can reach the site send one crafted request to its XML-RPC address and, in the worst case, run their own code, without logging in. Default installs from 4.0.0 through 6.1.5 are affected, even with XML-RPC switched off. Apache rates it Critical (CVSS 9.8) and says it is being actively exploited, and CISA added it to its exploited list (KEV) on 20 Nov 2026; one researcher's public code reaches the bug but says running code on a stock, up-to-date setup needs extra work. 6.1.6 (24 Sep 2026) and later fix it.
detail.meterHint: Attackers are already on it. Patch now.

checklist.text: ✓ On CISA's exploited list (fix by 23 Nov) 9

affected.title: Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5
affected.body: It's one bug with two CVEs: CVE-2026-129448 covers 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, and CVE-2026-82384 (25 Sep 2026) covers 6.1.5. 6.1.6 and later are fixed. Some news sites name 6.1.5 as the fix; Apache says 6.1.6. 1,2,4

affected.title: XML-RPC extensions still on
affected.body: Every release up to 6.1.5 ships with enabledForExtensions set to true and /roller-services/xmlrpc mapped, so default installs are exposed. Turning XML-RPC off in the admin settings (off by default) does not help. Run this in Roller's webapp folder; <param-value>true</param-value> means exposed. 1,2,7,8 grep -A1 enabledForExtensions WEB-INF/web.xml

affected.title: Attackers can reach the site
affected.body: One web request to /roller-services/xmlrpc is enough. No login and no user action are needed. 1,3

actions.title: Upgrade to Roller 6.1.7
actions.body: 6.1.6 (24 Sep 2026) fixes this bug; 6.1.7 (11 Nov 2026) is the newest and also fixes CVE-2026-123374, a separate deserialization bug in ping responses. Read the 6.1.7 behaviour changes first: for example, Planet is now off by default. Apache doesn't patch older lines. 4,5,6,12,13 Latest safe versions checked 20 Nov Apache Roller → 6.1 6.1.7 Apache fixes only the current release line. On anything older, upgrade to the newest 6.1 release.

actions.title: Can't upgrade yet?
actions.body: In WEB-INF/web.xml , set enabledForExtensions to false , or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping. Then restart Roller. The admin-screen switch alone is not enough. 1

actions.title: Look for signs of attack
actions.body: Attacks are POST requests to /roller-services/xmlrpc . Apache hasn't published other signs, attacker details or how many sites were hit. If you were exposed, check the server for changes you didn't make. 1,10

cves.name: vCenter zero-day
cves.line: Exploited in the wild, on KEV. No workaround.

detail.name: vCenter zero-day
detail.verdictHint: Exploited in the wild, on KEV. No workaround.
detail.summary: A bug in VMware vCenter's directory service lets anyone who can reach vCenter over the network get an administrator session without a password. Mandiant says a suspected China-nexus group, ARMORY CASTLE, exploited it in early September to create a rogue admin account and steal vCenter's login-signing key, and CISA added it to its exploited list on 20 Nov 2026. Broadcom fixed it on 19 Nov and gives no workaround; for vCenter 7.0 it lists no public fix and tells extended-support customers to contact Broadcom Support.
detail.meterHint: Attackers are already on it. Patch now.

checklist.text: ✓ On CISA's exploited list (fix by 23 Nov) 3

affected.title: vCenter before the fix
affected.body: Below 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 or 8.0 U3m. On VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x, you're affected until vCenter is on 8.0 U3m, which VCF 5.2.5 includes (for Telco Cloud, see Broadcom KB463116). vCenter 7.0 is affected too, and Mandiant says the attackers' tool works on 7.x and 8.x; Broadcom says to presume 6.5 and 6.7 are affected. The bug is in vCenter's directory service; Broadcom's FAQ says ESX isn't affected. 1,2,4,5

affected.title: An attacker can reach vCenter
affected.body: Network access to vCenter is enough; no login is needed. In the attack Mandiant investigated, the attackers first broke into another machine on the internal network, then reached vCenter's single sign-on port 2012 from there. 1,2

actions.title: Patch now
actions.body: Install 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 or 8.0 U3m (on VCF 5.x, patch vCenter to 8.0 U3m or move to VCF 5.2.5); Broadcom's patches are cumulative, so later versions also fix it. Broadcom gives no workaround. CISA's deadline for US agencies is 23 Nov 2026. Heads-up from Broadcom: 8.0 U3m and 9.0.2.0200 block upgrades to VCF 9.1.1, so patch now and wait for 9.1.2 before that upgrade (or move vCenter to 9.1.1 first and patch there). The same advisory also covers four lesser bugs that need an account or local access, in SDDC Manager and VMware Tools for Windows (CVE-2026-123891 to CVE-2026-123894), with their own fixed versions. 1,3,5 Latest safe versions checked 22 Nov VMware vCenter → 9.1 9.1.1.0200 9.0 9.0.2.0200 8.0 8.0 U3m VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x: patch vCenter to 8.0 U3m, or move to VCF 5.2.5, which includes it.

actions.title: On vCenter 7.0?
actions.body: Broadcom lists no public fix for 7.0 and tells customers with an extended support contract to contact Broadcom Support to request patches. Without one, there is no fix for 7.0. 1,5

actions.title: Limit who can reach vCenter
actions.body: Mandiant recommends a default-deny firewall on vCenter that allows its management ports, including 443 and 2012, only from an allowlist of trusted hosts. In its write-up, allowlisting port 2012 would have stopped the exploit, and allowlisting 443 would have stopped the attackers using the logins they forged. This adds protection; it doesn't replace the patch. 2

actions.title: Check for a break-in
actions.body: Patching doesn't remove attackers who are already in, and CISA flags this one for forensic triage. Look for single sign-on administrator accounts you didn't create, and for Mandiant's file indicators, such as /tmp/123 , /tmp/sss , /tmp/dbr and /usr/bin/vmtoolscs , on other internal Linux machines the attackers took over. The attackers also took vCenter's SAML signing key, which lets them forge logins for any user. 2,3

detail.summary: A bug in the Brotli decompressor, built into Node.js, .NET, Envoy and many Python apps, can crash your app, leak memory or possibly run code. detail.verdictHint: Exploited, no login. Axis bug in KEV, due 21 Nov.
detail.summary: A public exploit chain gives an attacker root on on-prem N-central servers that have the old Legacy API turned on, with no login. It gets in through an Apache Axis bug (CVE-2026-90436); the N-central root step has no CVE yet. Security firm Huntback found crypto miners on 21 servers within hours, and N-able reported attacks on 13 Nov.
detail.meterHint: Attackers are already on it. Patch now.

affected.title: On-prem N-central below 2026.4 HF3
affected.body: Hotfix 2 (2026.4.1.26, 10 Nov) does not stop this chain; the exploit was tested on it. Hotfix 3 (2026.4.1.39, 16 Nov) removes the Legacy API. N-able says hosted N-central is not vulnerable to the server chain and gets HF3 automatically. 3,4,5,6

affected.title: Legacy API is enabled
affected.body: Off by default, but admins can turn it on under Administration > Mail and Network Settings > Network Security > LEGACY APIS. N-able and the researcher agree the server chain needs it on and reachable. 3,4,8

affected.title: Attacker can reach the server
affected.body: No login needed: the Axis bug fires while the SOAP request is parsed, before any per-service auth runs. N-able says the server chain needs the Legacy API enabled and exposed to the internet. 7,4

actions.title: Upgrade to 2026.4 HF3 (2026.4.1.39)
actions.body: Rapid7 says apply it as an emergency, outside normal patch cycles. HF3 permanently blocks the Legacy API and fixes 17 new CVEs. Also update all Agents and Probes to 2026.4.1 HF3, and Patch Management Engine to 2.14.4.5829 or later. 4,5,6 Latest safe versions checked 20 Nov N-able N-central → Server 2026.4 2026.4.1.39 (HF3) Agents and Probes 2026.4.1 HF3 Patch Management Engine 2.14.4.5829 Agents and Probes have no published build number.

actions.title: Until then: turn off Legacy API
actions.body: Make sure the LEGACY APIS setting is off, even on HF2. If you truly need it, never expose it to the internet. 4,5,8

actions.title: Hunt for compromise
actions.body: Look in web logs for requests to /dms/services/ServerUI that mention jline.internal.TerminalLineSettings , an unexpected xvd.service unit, mining processes, files in /tmp/.xvd or /var/tmp/.xvd , and traffic to 157.20.241[.]16. If found, treat the server as fully owned (root). 3,4 systemctl status xvd.service; ls -la /tmp/.xvd /var/tmp/.xvd

actions.title: Then clean up downstream
actions.body: A hacked RMM server reaches every managed client. Rotate secrets stored in Automation Manager policies, enforce MFA on N-central accounts, and review activity from 11 Nov on for new accounts, scripts, scheduled tasks and remote sessions. The same Axis bug was also exploited against Confluence Data Center on 13 Nov. 4,5

detail.name: SSHole
detail.verdictHint: Exploited, in CISA KEV. Alpine-style sshd only.
detail.summary: On Linux systems that use musl libc and run sshd without PAM, mainly Alpine, an attacker can log in to password-less accounts (key-only users, Alpine's cloud alpine user) just by sending a very long password. Attacks started within hours of disclosure on 5 Nov 2026. Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and other glibc systems aren't affected.
detail.meterHint: Attackers are already on it. Patch now.

affected.title: sshd uses musl libc
affected.body: Alpine and other musl-based systems, including Alpine containers that run sshd. glibc systems (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, RHEL) and Dropbear are not affected. A line with ld-musl means musl. 2,5,7 ldd "$(command -v sshd)" | grep -i musl

affected.title: PAM off, password login on
affected.body: Alpine's openssh-server is built without PAM, so sshd -T prints no usepam line. openssh-server-pam with UsePAM yes is safe. passwordauthentication yes is the default. Run as root. 1,2,8 sshd -T | grep -Ei '^(passwordauthentication|usepam|permitrootlogin) '

affected.title: A * account plus a real hash
affected.body: Some account has * as its password (key-only users, root since about Alpine 3.16 if PermitRootLogin yes , the alpine user in cloud images 3.18.11–3.24.3) and at least one account has a $5$ or $6$ hash. Directory-service users (nslcd, winbind, sssd) with no shadow entry also count, and the commands below miss them. Locked ! accounts are safe. Run as root; the second command counts real hashes. 2 awk -F: '$2=="*"{print $1}' /etc/shadow; grep -cE '^[^:]*:\$[56]\$' /etc/shadow

affected.title: openssh below the fixed package
affected.body: Upstream: OpenSSH before 10.6p2. Alpine's fixed packages are listed under Upgrade. 9,2 apk info -v | grep '^openssh'

actions.title: Upgrade openssh, then restart
actions.body: Install the fixed package for your Alpine branch (listed below; fixes go back to 3.16). Run apk upgrade -U -a , then rc-service sshd restart : upgrading alone leaves the old sshd running. Other musl builds: OpenSSH 10.6p2. 1,2,3 Latest safe versions checked 20 Nov OpenSSH → Upstream 10.6p2 Alpine edge 10.6_p2-r0 Alpine 3.24 10.3_p1-r2 Alpine 3.23 10.2_p1-r1 Alpine 3.22 10.0_p1-r11 Alpine 3.21 9.9_p2-r1 Alpine 3.20 9.7_p1-r6 Alpine 3.19 9.6_p1-r3 Alpine 3.16 to 3.18 are fixed too: 9.0_p1-r6, 9.1_p1-r7, 9.3_p2-r4.

actions.title: Can't upgrade? Turn off passwords
actions.body: In sshd_config (or a drop-in in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ on Alpine 3.19+). Also set any PasswordAuthentication yes inside Match blocks to no; a drop-in doesn't override those. Check key login works, validate with sshd -t , then restart sshd and confirm sshd -T shows passwordauthentication no . 2 PasswordAuthentication no

actions.title: Look for break-ins
actions.body: A password login for root , alpine or any key-only user is a red flag. Also review doas use, new users, new authorized_keys entries and changed files. If you can't rule out a login, treat the host as compromised. US federal agencies must also do forensic triage under the KEV listing. 2,4 grep 'Accepted password for' /var/log/messages

detail.name: LiteLLM RCE
detail.verdictHint: In CISA KEV, due 2 Dec. Public PoC, needs admin key.
detail.summary: LiteLLM's proxy has an endpoint for testing custom guardrail code, and its home-made sandbox can be escaped to run any command, as root in the default Docker image. It needs a proxy-admin key, but attackers have been guessing default keys, and two other bugs let ordinary users become admin on older versions.
detail.meterHint: Attackers are already on it. Patch now.

checklist.text: Needs a LiteLLM admin key first 3,4
✓ On CISA's exploited list (fix by 2 Dec) 1,2

affected.title: LiteLLM 1.81.8 – 1.83.10
affected.body: GitHub's advisory lists >= 1.81.8, < 1.83.10 as affected, but its text says the fix is in 1.83.11, so count 1.83.10 as affected to be safe. Only the proxy server is at risk, not plain use of the Python SDK. In Docker, image tags don't reliably match versions ( main-latest tells you nothing), so check the pip version inside the container. 3,5 pip show litellm

affected.title: Management API is reachable
affected.body: The attacker can reach the proxy's management API, including POST /guardrails/test_custom_code . Keep it off untrusted networks. 3,4 docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Image}}' | grep -i litellm

affected.title: Attacker has an admin key
affected.body: The default config requires a proxy-admin credential (the master key). These also count: a weak key like sk-1234 ; no master key at all (callers are treated as admin); any user account below 1.83.14 (CVE-2026-47101/47102) or on 1.91.0 up to the CVE-2026-114612 fix; Enterprise-licensed proxies below 1.106.5, which can leak the master key to anyone; and proxies below 1.106.9 with an Azure model but no Azure API key set, where any logged-in user can read the master key. 3,5,6,7,11,12,13,16

actions.title: Upgrade to the newest on your line
actions.body: 1.83.11 fixed this sandbox escape, but later releases had their own admin-takeover bugs. Use at least 1.106.9, 1.108.6 or 1.109.1 (listed below). These also cover the older LiteLLM KEV entries CVE-2026-42208 and CVE-2026-42271 (fixed 1.83.7) and CVE-2026-59822 (fixed 1.84.0). 3,11,12,16,14,15,10 Latest safe versions checked 22 Nov LiteLLM → 1.110 1.110.2 1.109 1.109.3 1.108 (LTS) 1.108.15 1.106 1.106.12 Releases older than 1.106 have no fix: move up.

actions.title: Until then: block the endpoint
actions.body: Block POST /guardrails/test_custom_code at your reverse proxy or API gateway. Keep the admin port off the internet. If you use Azure models, also block the fields tenant_id , client_id , client_secret , azure_username , azure_password and azure_scope in request bodies. 3,4,16

actions.title: Rotate a weak or old master key
actions.body: Attackers sprayed default-style keys at this endpoint. If yours is guessable or was exposed, replace it. The escape exposes provider and cloud keys stored in the proxy, so rotate those too. 5

actions.title: Run the container as non-root
actions.body: The default image runs as root, so a sandbox escape gets root. LiteLLM also ships a non-root image. 3,5

detail.kicker: SAP ICM / Web Dispatcher · CVE-2026-76964 · CVE-2026-89126
detail.name: SAP ICM2SHELL
detail.verdictHint: If SAP's web ports are reachable. No attacks yet.
detail.summary: A memory bug in how SAP's built-in web server handles WebSocket traffic lets an attacker with no login leak server memory or run code as the SAP admin user (<sid>adm). It hits the ICM in NetWeaver AS ABAP and every SAP Web Dispatcher, including the one in HANA XS, and WebSocket support is on by default. SAP rates it 10.0 and fixed it on 10 Nov 2026; Onapsis ("ICM2SHELL") and nullFaktor ("SAPBleed") both built working exploits but haven't published them, and no attacks are reported.
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

affected.title: Kernel or Web Dispatcher not patched
affected.body: AS ABAP on kernel 7.40 or newer (7.22 isn't affected) and every Web Dispatcher. Fixed in 7.53 PL 1616, 7.54 PL 710, 7.77 PL 914, 7.93 PL 420 (or the updated-stack PL 401; PL 419 is still affected), 9.16 PL 111, 9.18 PL 37 and 9.20 PL 11. HANA 2.0 Web Dispatcher: 2.00.079.11 or 2.00.089.05; XS Advanced 1.0 SP05: Patch 4. Out-of-maintenance kernels (7.40, 7.41, 7.42, 7.45, 7.49, 7.73, 7.81, 7.85, 7.89) get no fix. AS Java alone isn't affected; dual-stack systems are. Check each server's kernel patch level in transaction SM51. 2,5,6,8

affected.title: WebSocket upgrades are on
affected.body: On by default in both the ICM and the Web Dispatcher, whether or not you use WebSockets. Not affected if icm/HTTP/support_websocket_upgrade is set to FALSE . 2,3

affected.title: Attackers can reach its web port
affected.body: Anyone who can reach the ICM or Web Dispatcher HTTP or HTTPS port can attack it; no SAP user or click is needed. An unpatched Web Dispatcher in front of the ICM doesn't stop the attack and can pass it on to internal systems. 3,4,5

actions.title: Apply SAP Notes 3778530 and 3778556
actions.body: Patch the kernel (ICM) and every Web Dispatcher, including HANA XS, to the fixed patch level for your release, then restart. On an out-of-maintenance kernel, move to a supported kernel first. 1,2 Latest safe versions checked 20 Nov SAP kernel and Web Dispatcher → Kernel 9.20 9.20 PL 11 Kernel 9.18 9.18 PL 37 Kernel 9.16 9.16 PL 111 Kernel 7.93 7.93 PL 420 Kernel 7.77 7.77 PL 914 Kernel 7.54 7.54 PL 710 Kernel 7.53 7.53 PL 1616 HANA 2.0 Rev. 089 (XS) 2.00.089.05 HANA 2.0 Rev. 079 (XS) 2.00.079.11 Kernel 7.22 isn't affected. XS Advanced 1.0 SP05 is fixed in Patch 4.

actions.title: Can't patch? Turn off WebSocket
actions.body: Set this parameter in the ICM and Web Dispatcher profiles and restart. It breaks ABAP Push Channels and some Fiori apps, so first look for status code 101 in the ICM or Web Dispatcher HTTP log. SAP's FAQ Note 3778788 says where the parameter goes for each component. 2,3 icm/HTTP/support_websocket_upgrade = FALSE

actions.title: Or shield behind a patched Web Dispatcher
actions.body: A Web Dispatcher on 7.53 PL 1629, 7.54 PL 723, 7.93 PL 430, 9.16 PL 200 or later protects systems behind it, but only if nothing can reach them directly (check with a network scan) and it isn't set up with PROT=ROUTER . 2,8

cves.name: Upload2Shell
cves.line: Outsiders' files reach it. Full exploit announced.

detail.name: Upload2Shell
detail.verdictHint: Outsiders' files reach it. Full exploit announced.
detail.summary: A bug in Ghostscript before 10.08.0 lets a crafted file escape Ghostscript's -dSAFER sandbox and run commands as the account doing the rendering. The file holds PostScript but can be uploaded as an image named .png or .jpg : image libraries such as ImageMagick and Pillow pick the format from the content and hand it to Ghostscript, which also runs behind email thumbnails and print servers; the researchers ran commands through Debian's CUPS, Roundcube, WordPress and more. The CVE record scores it as a local attack (8.5), but those routes are remote. The researchers published a proof of concept that does most of the work: it takes control of Ghostscript's memory (tested on 10.07.0, x86-64 Linux), and their write-up shows the remaining steps to running commands in excerpts; one of them relies on memory offsets from the researchers' test build. They say a full exploit for the Debian CUPS route comes next. No attacks are reported yet.
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

affected.title: Ghostscript before 10.08.0
affected.body: Distros backport the fix without changing gs --version , so check the package instead: fixed in Debian 12 10.0.0~dfsg-11+deb12u9 , Debian 13 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u2 , Ubuntu 24.04 10.02.1~dfsg1-0ubuntu7.10 and 22.04 9.55.0~dfsg1-0ubuntu5.15 (newer releases too; older ones through Ubuntu Pro). Ubuntu's notice USN-8949-1 lists this bug as "No CVE number" (the researchers link it to this CVE), while Ubuntu's CVE tracker still says "Needs evaluation" for every release. No fixed package yet on 22 Nov 2026: Amazon Linux 2, 2023 and 2027 Preview ("Pending Fix"), SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 and 16 ("In progress"), openSUSE Leap 16 ("Affected"). The 10.08.0 release candidate (18 Aug) also calls itself 10.08.0 but came before the fixes, so check it isn't what you run. Container images carry their own copy. 1,3,4,6,7,15,16,17,23,24 gs --version

affected.title: It renders files from outsiders
affected.body: Something passes files you don't control to Ghostscript. Common routes: image or PDF previews through ImageMagick/Imagick, Pillow (EPS files, once pixels are loaded) or libvips with ImageMagick loaders; these check the file's content, not its name, so a .png upload counts. It doesn't have to be a PDF: the researcher says an image or a video can carry it (the write-up tests images and documents, not video). Also: Roundcube attachment thumbnails (before 1.6.20 / 1.7.5), WordPress uploads by Authors and up or public plugin upload forms (before 7.0.4 / 6.9.7), CUPS print queues shared without a login, and document importers that convert PDFs. On a desktop, the CVE record's score assumes a user opens the file. 1,2,3,8,13,14,20

actions.title: Outsiders' files reach it? Update now
actions.body: Upload forms, previews, email thumbnails, shared print queues: don't wait for attacks, because the public proof of concept and write-up cover most of an exploit. Update to 10.08.0 or your distro's fixed package: Debian DLA-4914-1 and DSA-6516-1, Ubuntu USN-8949-1 (it lists the bug without a CVE number). This fixes every route at once. 10.08.0 also fixes five other Ghostscript CVEs (CVE-2026-110133, -112922, -103226, -19547 and -39919); Artifex's own CVE list doesn't name this one. One of them, CVE-2026-39919, is a JPEG 2000 overflow in PDFs; Wordfence's two exploits for it only worked on the exact Ghostscript build they were made for, Wordfence hasn't published them, and no attacks are reported. Amazon Linux, SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 and 16, and openSUSE Leap 16 have no fixed package yet: cut the route (below) until they do. Rebuild container images that install Ghostscript. 3,4,5,6,7,15,16,18,19,21,22,23 Latest safe versions checked 22 Nov Ghostscript → 10.08 10.08.0 Artifex lists a single current release. Linux distros backport fixes into older versions (Debian 12's fixed package is still 10.0.0), so check your distro's advisory.

actions.title: Update the apps that reach it
actions.body: WordPress 7.0.4 or 6.9.7 (fixes go back to 4.7) closes the upload route as CVE-2026-65640. Roundcube 1.6.20 or 1.7.5 stops passing EPS and SVG to ImageMagick (CVE-2026-114727). These help, but the Ghostscript update fixes the bug itself. 8,9,14 Latest safe versions checked 22 Nov WordPress → 7.1 7.1.5 7.0 7.0.9 6.9 6.9.12 6.8 6.8.13 Older branches back to 4.7 also get security releases (for example 6.7.12); 4.6 and older get none. Only the newest version is actively supported, and sites with automatic background updates on get these by themselves.

actions.title: Print servers: require a login
actions.body: Requiring authentication on a shared CUPS queue blocked the researchers' anonymous print job. 3

actions.title: Can't update yet? Cut the route
actions.body: ImageMagick: its security policy docs show this policy.xml line to stop it running Ghostscript and other external delegates (ImageMagick 7.0.1-8 and later). Python: pass formats=["PNG", "JPEG"] (whatever you accept) to Pillow's Image.open() so EPS is never loaded. Neither covers print servers or apps that call gs directly. 11,12,13 <policy domain="delegate" rights="none" pattern="*"/>

actions.body: Attacks reported, the researchers' announced full exploit (the Debian CUPS route) or another one published, or a listing on CISA's exploited list (KEV). 3,10

cves.name: SGLang RCE
cves.line: Exploited, no fix yet. Risky if the port is reachable.

detail.name: SGLang RCE
detail.verdictHint: Exploited, no fix yet. Risky if the port is reachable.
detail.summary: SGLang, a popular server for running AI models, has unfixed bugs that let anyone who can reach its port run code or steal its API keys, mostly without logging in. On 9 Nov 2026 NEAR AI said an attacker used an SGLang code-execution bug, which it hasn't named, to break into an inference server. There's no fix yet, so keep SGLang off untrusted networks.
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

affected.title: You run SGLang (any version)
affected.body: The CVE record for CVE-2026-15969 lists v0.5.15 and earlier, but no fixed version has been named. As of 20 Nov 2026 the advisories still list no patched version, and v0.5.23 (2 Nov) is the newest release. Treat every version as affected. 3,6,7,8 pip show sglang

affected.title: Its HTTP port is reachable by attackers
affected.body: By default SGLang listens only on 127.0.0.1, port 30000. You're exposed if it was started with --host 0.0.0.0, published from a container or Kubernetes, or put behind a proxy that forwards every route. API keys alone don't close it: the LoRA tensor route has no auth check when LoRA is on, and /server_info can leak the keys. Admin routes are open when no keys are set. Changes merged on 7 and 14 Nov stop /server_info leaking keys and make admin routes need an admin key (the current docs already describe this), but no release includes them yet. 4,5,11,12 ss -ltnp | grep 30000

actions.title: Keep SGLang off untrusted networks
actions.body: Bind it to 127.0.0.1 or a private network, segment inference hosts, and firewall the port. If clients must reach it, put a reverse proxy in front that allows only the inference routes you use and blocks everything else, including /server_info. 2,4,8

actions.title: Set separate user and admin API keys
actions.body: Start with both --api-key and --admin-api-key, and block /server_info, which gives the admin key to anyone holding the user key. This doesn't fix the LoRA tensor bug, so it's no substitute for network limits. 4,5

actions.title: Turn off pickle IPC and unused features
actions.body: Set SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC to false (it defaults to true). Don't enable LoRA, the dumper (DUMPER_SERVER_PORT), remote weight updates or distributed weight routes unless you need them. Prefer safetensors and refuse untrusted .bin/.pt checkpoints. 2,4

actions.title: Was it exposed? Rotate keys, check logs
actions.body: /server_info returns the API keys and SSL key password, so rotate them. Make sure API keys and prompts aren't written to logs; NEAR AI lost two customers' API keys that way. Watch for an upstream fix and update when one ships. 1,4,8

cves.name: nginx2root
cves.line: Public exploit for HTTP/2. Same fix covers 9 more bugs.

detail.name: nginx2root
detail.verdictHint: Public exploit for HTTP/2. Same fix covers 9 more bugs.
detail.summary: A bug in nginx's HTTP/2 handling lets an attacker with no login crash nginx or run code as the nginx worker user, and a public exploit is out. Despite the name, it doesn't give root by itself (Xint got root by chaining it with a separate Linux kernel bug, covered on our Linux SCTP root page), and code execution needs ASLR to be off or bypassed. The same 18 Nov releases fix nine more nginx bugs, including the other four Xint groups as nginx2root (a second HTTP/2 bug, HTTP/3, resolver and mail proxy) and a TLS 1.3 hang; turning off HTTP/2 covers only the two HTTP/2 bugs.
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

affected.title: nginx before 1.31.9 / 1.30.7
affected.body: Stable 1.30.7 and later are fixed. Also NGINX Plus 37.0 before 37.0.8.1 and 37.1 before 37.3.0.1 (37.2.x included); older NGINX Plus R33–R36 get no fix (sources differ on R33), so move to 37.x. Distros backport fixes without changing nginx -v , so check the package against your distro's advisory. After upgrading, restart: a reload keeps the old binary. 1,3,8,5,9 nginx -v

affected.title: You use an affected feature
affected.body: HTTP/2 ( http2 on; or listen ... http2 , on any server block) is the one with a public exploit; static-only sites count, and behind a proxy that terminates HTTP/2 the exploit likely fails but the bug is still there. The same upgrade fixes bugs in HTTP/3 ( listen ... quic ) with proxy_pass ; resolver with a variable in proxy_pass plus a mirror or SSI subrequest; the mail proxy with proxy on and auth_http ; and HTTPS servers using TLS 1.3, where a worker can hang (CVE-2026-118899). Smaller stream and try_files bugs are in the bug list. 1,3,4,5,18,19,20,21 sudo nginx -T 2>&1 | grep -nE 'http2|quic|resolver|mirror|ssi on|auth_http'

actions.title: Can't upgrade? Turn off what you can

HTTP/3: remove quic from listen and set http3 off; . Resolver: point proxy_pass at a fixed upstream and turn off mirror ; Xint says turning off mirror alone isn't enough. Mail proxy: bind its listeners to 127.0.0.1 or firewall them. F5 gives no workaround for the TLS 1.3 hang. 1,5,18,19,20,21 http2 off;

cves.line: Public exploit: cat a file, run commands. Get 3.7.9.

detail.name: iTerm2 cmd exec
detail.verdictHint: Public exploit: cat a file, run commands. Get 3.7.9.
detail.summary: In iTerm2 3.6.1 through 3.7.8, displaying a crafted file in the terminal, for example with cat README.md , runs commands on your Mac. The trap is hidden in the file (you only see some shell errors when it runs), and it works on a default install in bash, zsh and fish. The researcher published a complete exploit; iTerm2 fixed it in 3.7.9 on 20 Nov 2026. No attacks are reported. There's no fixed release for macOS 12.4 to 12.x, whose newest iTerm2 is 3.6.11. The researcher first called it remote code execution (RCE), then retitled it arbitrary command execution; since you have to display the attacker's file, it isn't remote in the usual sense.

detail.name: Linux TCP root
detail.verdictHint: Any IPv4 TCP server. Root shown only via MPTCP.
detail.summary: A race in the kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake code lets a remote attacker with no login corrupt kernel memory by sending connection requests that carry IP options. detail.name: Ruby2Shell
detail.verdictHint: Rails or classic Sinatra on old Ruby. No public exploit.
detail.summary: A one-byte memory bug in how Ruby changes the case of text in older Western encodings (like ISO-8859-1) may let an attacker with no login run code on the server. The researchers who named it say default Rails and classic-style Sinatra apps reach it. The fix is a Ruby upgrade, which also fixes six related regex and string bugs.
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

affected.body: Affected: 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0–3.4.12 and 4.0.0–4.0.9. Ruby 3.2 and older are end of life and won't get a fix. Check the Ruby your app actually runs (its container image or .ruby-version ), not just the system one. Distros may patch without changing the version; on 20 Nov Ubuntu (priority Medium) and Debian were still evaluating. 1,2,6,8,9 ruby -v

affected.title: Web input gets case-changed

cves.line: Only if FastCGI connections are reused. Fixed 19 Nov.

detail.name: PHP-FPM smuggling
detail.verdictHint: Only if FastCGI connections are reused. Fixed 19 Nov.
detail.summary: A bug in PHP-FPM can let an attacker with no login sneak a second, hidden request to PHP in one web request and run their own code. It only works where the web server reuses its connections to PHP-FPM (off by default in nginx and Apache) and the app opens the request body without reading all of it. PHP rates it Critical (CVSS 9.2); public test code runs PHP on a target, and the 19 Nov 2026 releases fix it.
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

affected.title: PHP-FPM older than the 19 Nov 2026 fix
affected.body: Below 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36. PHP 8.6.0 (19 Nov) is fixed. PHP says the bug has been in the code since 5.6.0, so older, unsupported PHP is affected too. The code-execution attack needs PHP-FPM; with LiteSpeed's LSAPI it only breaks later requests. Distros may backport the fix without changing the version number. 1,2,3,10 php-fpm -v

affected.title: The web server reuses FPM connections
affected.body: nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on , Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on , or HAProxy keeping FastCGI connections open. Both nginx and Apache close the connection by default, which is not affected, but Apache's own PHP-FPM example turns reuse on. PHP's advisory doesn't mention Caddy. For Apache, look for enablereuse=on in your config. 1,4,5 nginx -T 2>/dev/null | grep fastcgi_keep_conn

affected.title: The app leaves the body unread
affected.body: Some code path opens php://input and doesn't read it to the end. PHP says frameworks that open the input stream before routing or login checks can be affected; public test code worked against an unmodified Slim 4 app. Reading the body fully avoids it, but PHP says that isn't reliable on its own. 1,6

actions.body: Update to 8.6.0, 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (19 Nov 2026), then restart PHP-FPM. actions.title: Turn off connection reuse
actions.body: Until you've updated: in nginx, remove fastcgi_keep_conn on (off is the default); in Apache, remove enablereuse=on . Then reload the web server. 1,4,5 fastcgi_keep_conn off;

actions.body: Don't let untrusted networks reach PHP-FPM's port or socket directly. 1

cves.line: Only with mixed session serializers. Fixed 19 Nov.

detail.name: PHP session RCE
detail.verdictHint: Only with mixed session serializers. Fixed 19 Nov.
detail.summary: PHP's session upload-progress feature can let an attacker with no login run code, but only where sessions are written with one serializer and read with another, and the app has a suitable code library. PHP rates it Critical; exploit code for a test lab is public, and the 19 Nov 2026 releases fix it. It's a sibling of PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619).
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

affected.title: PHP older than the 19 Nov 2026 fix
affected.body: PHP 8.2 to 8.5 below 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36. PHP 8.6.0 (19 Nov) is fixed. The 21 Oct releases didn't fix this bug. Older, unsupported PHP may also be affected. Distros may backport the fix without changing the version number. 1,2,7 php -v

affected.title: Session upload progress is on
affected.body: In anything that can write to your session store. It was on by default before the fix; the fix turns it off by default, but an explicit setting in php.ini or a pool still wins. The CLI can read a different php.ini than PHP-FPM or Apache. 1,4 php -i | grep session.upload_progress.enabled

affected.title: Two serializers share sessions
affected.body: Something writes sessions with php_binary or php_serialize while something else reads the same sessions with php . For example, an app calls ini_set() before session_start(), or two apps, FPM pools, virtual hosts or CLI jobs with different settings share a session directory. PHP's 23 Oct notice described only the first case; the 19 Nov advisory says no runtime switch is needed. 1,3 php -i | grep session.serialize_handler

affected.title: The reader has a usable library
affected.body: Code execution needs a suitable "gadget chain" in the reading app. PHP's advisory demonstrates it with Guzzle and Monolog, both common in Composer apps. Without one, the bug can still corrupt sessions or crash requests. 1

actions.title: Update PHP and restart
actions.body: Update to 8.6.0, 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (19 Nov 2026), then restart every PHP worker. Debian has fixed packages (DSA-6641-1, DLA-4916-1); Ubuntu hadn't shipped one by 20 Nov. The fix turns session upload progress off by default and blocks runtime changes to session settings while it's on. 1,2,7,9,10 Latest safe versions checked 22 Nov PHP → 8.6 8.6.0 8.5 8.5.13 8.4 8.4.28 8.3 8.3.37 8.2 8.2.36 PHP 8.1 and older get no fixes from PHP. Distros may backport fixes without changing the version number.

actions.title: Keep upload progress off
actions.body: Set it in php.ini, the FPM pool or server config, not with ini_set() (that's too late), then restart. Check that nothing explicitly turns it back on. 1,4 session.upload_progress.enabled = 0

actions.title: If you need upload progress
actions.body: Every app, pool and job that reads those sessions must use the same serialize_handler , even after updating. Otherwise give each app its own session storage, and expire old sessions when you change formats. 1

detail.name: phpAfterShell
detail.verdictHint: Needs a crashed session write and a gadget. Fixed 19 Nov.
detail.summary: PHP's default file-based session storage can leave a half-old, half-new session file if a write is cut short, and an attacker can use that to make PHP rebuild objects of their choice and run code. It also needs the attacker's data in the session, a worker killed mid-write and a suitable code library in the app; lab exploit code is public, no attacks are reported, and the 19 Nov 2026 releases fix it. It's a separate bug from PHP2Shell , not a bypass: the October releases just don't include this fix.

affected.body: PHP 8.2 to 8.5 below 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36. PHP 8.6.0 (19 Nov) is fixed. The October PHP2Shell releases don't fix it. PHP says the code dates back to PHP 4.1.0, so older, unsupported PHP is affected too. Distros may backport the fix without changing the version number. 1,2,3 php -v

affected.title: Sessions are stored in files
affected.body: The files save handler is PHP's default. Sessions in Redis, a database or another store that replaces a record in one step aren't hit by this bug. The CLI can read a different php.ini than PHP-FPM or Apache. 1,3 php -i | grep session.save_handler

affected.title: Attackers can fill the session
affected.body: They need to put a lot of their own data into a session. Session upload progress does that for anyone who sends a file upload, and it was on by default until the 19 Nov releases (see PHP session RCE ). An app that stores large user input in the session works too, even with upload progress off. Whether a login is needed depends on the app. 1,3,4 php -i | grep session.upload_progress.enabled

affected.title: The write can be cut short
affected.body: The PHP worker has to die partway through saving the session. PHP's advisory describes a memory-limit crash in another thread on threaded PHP builds; Wiz says memory limits or timeouts can do it. One public lab does it over plain HTTP by pushing a memory-limited container into an out-of-memory kill. 1,5,6

affected.title: The app has a usable library
affected.body: Running code needs a suitable "gadget chain" in the app, which isn't in every app. Both public labs plant their own gadget class. Without one, the bug can still corrupt sessions. 1,5,6,7

actions.title: Update PHP and restart
actions.body: Update to 8.6.0, 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (19 Nov 2026), then restart every PHP worker. The fix empties the session file before writing, so a cut-short write can lose a session but can't mix two. Debian has fixed packages (DSA-6641-1, DLA-4916-1). The same releases fix our other PHP pages, PHP session RCE and PHP-FPM smuggling . 1,2,8 Latest safe versions checked 22 Nov PHP → 8.6 8.6.0 8.5 8.5.13 8.4 8.4.28 8.3 8.3.37 8.2 8.2.36 PHP 8.1 and older get no fixes from PHP. actions.title: Optional: a different session store
actions.body: PHP says a store that replaces records in one step avoids this bug; depthfirst names Redis and databases. Updating PHP is still the recommended fix for the default files handler. 1,3

cves.name: Linux SCTP root
cves.line: Needs code on the box. No stable kernel fix yet.

detail.name: Linux SCTP root
detail.verdictHint: Needs code on the box. No stable kernel fix yet.
detail.summary: A bug in the Linux kernel's SCTP code lets any local user, including one inside a container, free the same kernel memory twice and take over the machine. Xint chained it with nginx2root to get root on the host and escape a Docker container. The fix reached the main kernel tree on 19 Nov, but no stable kernel has it yet and almost no distro ships it, so blocking the sctp module is the stopgap.
detail.meterHint: Find out if you're affected. If you are, patch.

checklist.text: Needs a way to run code on the machine or in one of its containers, as any user first 1,2

affected.title: Kernel 4.15 or later
affected.body: The bug arrived in 4.15 (Jan 2018). The fix was merged into the main kernel tree on 19 Nov, after 7.4-rc3. The newest stable kernels (7.3.5, 6.18.64, 6.12.118, released 17 Nov) don't have it, and on 22 Nov it wasn't queued for the next ones either; the only distro kernels we found carrying it are Gentoo's kernel sources and a Fedora Rawhide test build that hasn't shipped yet. Xint hasn't named the fix, but the commit credits Xint's tool and matches its description. 1,2,3,4,5,6,18,20,21 uname -r

affected.title: Untrusted code can run on it
affected.body: The attacker must already run code on the machine, as any user or inside a container. Xint got there through nginx2root. The bug needs no special rights. Containers don't stop it: they share the host kernel, Docker's default seccomp profile doesn't block SCTP sockets, and Kubernetes pods run without seccomp unless you turn it on. 1,2,9,12,13,14

affected.title: SCTP can load
affected.body: The kernel loads the sctp module the first time any program opens an SCTP socket, unless it's blocked. Many distros ship it. Red Hat says it isn't loaded by default on RHEL: it's in kernel-modules-extra, which blacklists it on install. If lsmod prints nothing, it can still load on demand; modprobe -c | grep sctp shows any block. 1,9,10,11,15 lsmod | grep sctp

actions.title: Block SCTP if you don't use it
actions.body: Put this line in a file under /etc/modprobe.d/ (Ubuntu uses disable-sctp.conf); on Debian and Ubuntu, then run sudo update-initramfs -u . It doesn't unload a module that's already loaded (reboot, or sudo rmmod sctp if nothing uses it) and doesn't help if SCTP is built into the kernel. It breaks telecom signalling and some Kubernetes network plugins. Red Hat's version is install sctp /bin/true plus blacklist sctp . 1,9,10,16 install sctp /bin/false

actions.title: Update the kernel and reboot
actions.body: Install your distro's kernel with the fix ("sctp: do not free a new asoc peeled off while sendmsg slept") once it ships, then reboot. No stable release has it as of 22 Nov, and it isn't queued for the next stable releases yet; Debian unstable's 7.3.5-1 doesn't have it either. 2,3,4,18,19

actions.title: Patch the way in
actions.body: Xint's chain starts with nginx2root, so upgrade nginx too. Any other way to run code on the host or in a container works just as well. 1,7

cves.line: SSH in as users with no stored password. Rare module.

detail.name: pam-mysql bypass
detail.verdictHint: SSH in as users with no stored password. Rare module.
detail.summary: pam-mysql, a rarely used module that checks Linux logins against a MySQL table, gets one check backwards. With sshd's default settings, anyone can log in over SSH as an account whose stored password is empty, typing any password. Debian fixed it on 19 Nov 2026; Ubuntu and Fedora haven't yet. The researcher demonstrated it but hasn't published the exploit, and no attacks are reported.
detail.meterHint: Patch on schedule. Watch for news.

affected.title: pam-mysql checks your logins
affected.body: The module is in the PAM setup of a login service such as sshd, the case the researcher tested. Every released version has the bug, 0.8.x and the 1.0.0 betas. Few systems use it: Debian counts 190 installs. A file name in the output means it's in use for that service. 1,10 grep -rl pam_mysql /etc/pam.d/

affected.title: The service refuses empty passwords
affected.body: That is sshd's default ( PermitEmptyPasswords no ), and it's what triggers the bug: sshd asks pam-mysql to refuse accounts with no password, and pam-mysql does the opposite. Don't switch it to yes as a fix; the researcher says that opens a different hole. Run as root. 1,5 sshd -T | grep -i permitemptypasswords

affected.title: Some accounts have no password
affected.body: At least one row in the login table has no stored password. On 0.8.x (Debian, Ubuntu, Gentoo, FreeBSD) that means NULL. On the 1.0.0 betas (Fedora, Nix, Mageia, ALT) an empty string counts too, so the common NOT NULL DEFAULT '' column is exposed; the researcher says PostfixAdmin and Froxlor ship tables like that. Replace the table and column names with yours. 1 SELECT username FROM users WHERE password IS NULL OR password='';
code: SELECT username FROM users WHERE password IS NULL OR password='';

affected.title: The package isn't patched
affected.body: Fixed: Debian 13 0.8.2-2.1+deb13u1 and Debian 12 0.8.2-2+deb12u1 . Some news sites give 0.8.2-2.1 as fixed for Debian 13; Debian lists that version as vulnerable. Not fixed yet on 21 Nov 2026: Debian testing and unstable, Ubuntu ("needs evaluation"), Fedora and Gentoo. On Fedora the package is pam_mysql . 2,3,4,8,11,9,12 dpkg -l libpam-mysql

actions.title: Update the package
actions.body: On Debian 12 and 13, install the update from DSA-6643-1 or DLA-4919-1. The fix adds a nullok option, off by default, so accounts with no password are refused. Elsewhere there's no fixed package yet: upstream fixed its 1.0 code on 19 Nov 2026 but hasn't tagged a release, and its 0.8.x branch has no fix. 2,3,1,6,7

actions.title: No update yet? Fill the gaps
actions.body: Remove or lock rows with no password in any table used for logins, then make the password column NOT NULL with no empty-string default. That's the researcher's fix for unpatched systems. Don't set PermitEmptyPasswords yes . 1

actions.title: Check past logins
actions.body: sshd logs a bypass exactly like a normal login ("Accepted password for"). Any password login by an account that had no stored password at the time was a bypass. The table as it is now may not show what it held then; a backup or the binary log does. pam-mysql's own log table is off by default, and when on it spells failures AUTHENTICATION FALURE . 1

cves.line: Only bites if a configured path ends in /. No exploit.

detail.name: Spring Boot slash
detail.verdictHint: Only bites if a configured path ends in /. No exploit.
detail.summary: Spring rates this Spring Boot bug Critical. Spring Boot builds security rules for Actuator endpoints and the H2 console from paths in your configuration; if such a path ends in a slash, the rule comes out wrong and doesn't match the real endpoint, which can then be left unsecured. The fix only strips that slash, so paths without one behave the same before and after. Free fixes exist only for Spring Boot 4.0 and 4.1.
detail.meterHint: Patch on schedule. Watch for news.

affected.title: Spring Boot 4.1.2 or older

affected.title: Rules use EndpointRequest or the H2 console matcher
affected.body: Your Spring Security config builds rules with EndpointRequest (Actuator, servlet or reactive) or PathRequest.toH2Console() . The fix didn't change the static-resource matchers. 1,2

affected.title: A configured path ends in /
affected.body: For example management.endpoints.web.path-mapping.health=status/ or spring.h2.console.path=/custom/ , which produce a rule for /actuator/status//** that never matches /actuator/status . The fix also covers health group additional paths and / as the Actuator base path. Look for those properties and check whether a value ends in a slash. 2 grep -rnE "path-mapping|console.path|base-path|additional-path" src/main/resources/

affected.title: A later rule is looser
affected.body: Spring Security checks rules in order and uses the first that matches. When the broken rule doesn't match, the request falls through to your next rule, so the endpoint is only left open if that rule is looser, for example anyRequest().permitAll() . 4,1

The two GitHub "exploits" going around are a version checker and an unverified guess written without seeing Oracle's fix, and no attacks have been reported.

affected.title: MySQL 8.4, 9.7 or 26.10
affected.body: Oracle lists MySQL Server 8.4.0 to 8.4.13, 9.7.0 to 9.7.4 and 26.10, and MySQL Cluster 8.0.0 to 8.0.50, 8.4.0 to 8.4.13, 9.7.0 to 9.7.4 and 26.10. Server 8.0 isn't listed because Oracle no longer supports it, not because it was checked, so TuxCare treats it as possibly affected. Oracle files the bug under "Client programs", so machines with only the mysql command-line tools count too. MariaDB and Percona haven't said whether they're affected; Red Hat lists its hardened MariaDB 10.11 and 11.8 images as affected. 1,7,8 mysql --version

affected.title: An attacker reaches the MySQL traffic
affected.body: Oracle says the attack goes over the MySQL network protocol, with no login and no user action. It hasn't said whether the server or a client program connecting to a server is the side at risk. "A client connecting to a malicious server" is analysts' guess, not something Oracle has confirmed. The sources also disagree on the kind of bug: CISA's data says improper authentication (CWE-287), Red Hat says missing authentication (CWE-306). 1,7,15,2,8

actions.title: Nothing urgent yet
actions.body: There's no confirmed exploit and no reported attack, it isn't on CISA's exploited list, and CISA's own assessment says exploitation "none". The 19 Nov GitHub code is a fake MySQL server that captures passwords from clients connecting without encryption; its author says Oracle's fix isn't public, so nothing ties it to this bug. We'll change the verdict if Oracle, the researcher or a distro explains the bug, if real exploit code or attacks appear, or if it lands on CISA's list. 2,14,12,11,13,7

actions.title: Update when the fix ships
actions.body: The fixed builds 8.4.13.1, 9.7.4.1 and 26.10.0.1 are listed as not yet released, with no date. Until then the fix is only available to Oracle support customers through My Oracle Support. Oracle's next scheduled updates are on 15 Dec 2026 and 19 Jan 2027; nobody has said the public fix ships in either. Distros disagree on severity: Red Hat rates it Critical, Ubuntu Medium. Debian, Red Hat and Ubuntu have no fixed packages yet. 4,5,6,7,8,9,10

detail.name: Tomcat Nov release
detail.verdictHint: CISA says 9.1, Apache says Low. Off-by-default features.
detail.summary: Apache disclosed 11 Tomcat vulnerabilities on 19 Nov 2026: 1 critical, 4 important, 2 moderate and 4 low. All but one need a feature you have to turn on, such as HTTP/2, the RewriteValve or clustering, and none has a public exploit or reported attacks. The "9.1 critical" posts come from scores CISA added to the CVE records; Apache rates that bug Low. Fixed releases are out for all but two cluster bugs.
detail.meterHint: Patch on schedule. Watch for news.

affected.title: Tomcat before 11.0.29 / 10.1.62 / 9.0.124
affected.body: Every earlier 11.0, 10.1 and 9.0 release; end-of-life 8.5 and older get no fixes. The critical cluster bug is the exception: it affects only 11.0.29, 10.1.62 and 9.0.124. Spring Boot embeds Tomcat, and its newest releases (4.2.0, 4.1.3 and 4.0.10) still bring in 11.0.27; check with ./mvnw dependency:tree -Dincludes=org.apache.tomcat.embed . 1,2,3,13,14 $CATALINA_HOME/bin/version.sh

affected.title: You turned on an affected feature
affected.body: Ten of the 11 need something you add: HTTP/2 (an Http2Protocol line inside a <Connector> ; in Spring Boot, server.http2.enabled ), the RewriteValve, the ExpiresFilter, CGI, Jakarta Authentication, clustering, an AJP load balancer or the OWB module. The shipped files contain commented-out examples, so matches inside <!-- --> don't count. Check your apps' WEB-INF/web.xml and META-INF/context.xml too. The eleventh, a low-rated memory leak (CVE-2026-118233), needs an app that uses the HTTP upgrade API; Apache only says "some circumstances". 1,10,11,16,17 grep -rnE 'Http2Protocol|RewriteValve|ExpiresFilter|CGIServlet|<Cluster|LoadBalancerDrainingValve|OpenWebBeans' $CATALINA_BASE/conf/

actions.title: Upgrade to 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124
actions.body: Released 13 to 16 Nov 2026, these fix 10 of the 11 bugs. Tomcat 8.5 gets no fixes (end of life since 31 Mar 2024), and 9.0 support ends on 31 Mar 2027. 12,13,1,2,3 Latest safe versions checked 22 Nov Apache Tomcat → 11.0 11.0.29 10.1 10.1.62 9.0 9.0.124 Tomcat 8.5 reached end of life on 31 Mar 2024 and gets no fixes; 10.0 and older are also unsupported. Spring Boot embeds Tomcat and pins its own version.

actions.title: Spring Boot: set the Tomcat version
actions.body: No Spring Boot release brings in a fixed Tomcat yet. Set the tomcat.version property to 11.0.29 in your build, the documented way to override a version Spring Boot manages. HTTP/2 is off unless you set server.http2.enabled . 14,15,16

actions.title: Clusters: stay on TLS 1.2
actions.body: If your cluster uses TLS-PSK, keep it on TLS 1.2: on TLS 1.3 a node without the key can join (CVE-2026-133325). The fix comes in 11.0.30, 10.1.63 and 9.0.125; Apache hasn't announced a date, and we'll check again by 28 Nov 2026. The old EncryptInterceptor won't be fixed (CVE-2026-95517): move to TLS-PSK on TLS 1.2. 7,8,1

actions.title: Don't panic over the 9.1
actions.body: The scary numbers come from CISA's automated scoring added to the CVE records, not from Apache: 9.1 on CVE-2026-116561, which Apache rates Low, meaning "extremely hard to exploit" or with "minimal consequences". Apache's own ratings: one critical (the cluster bug), four important. 5,4,6,1

cves.name: OpenSSL base64
cves.line: Needs ~1.6 GB of input you supply. No remote path known.

detail.name: OpenSSL base64
detail.verdictHint: Needs ~1.6 GB of input you supply. No remote path known.
detail.summary: A bug in OpenSSL 4.0 and 4.1 can write past the end of a buffer when a program asks it to base64-encode about 1.6 GB or more in one go. The only trigger described so far is the openssl s_client command given a huge proxy password by the person running it. The Critical 9.8 score comes from CISA, which assumes a remote attacker with no login; OpenSSL hasn't rated it yet, and Ubuntu rates it Medium.
detail.meterHint: Real, but not worth losing sleep over.

checklist.text: Needs control over ~1.6 GB of data an app base64-encodes first 2

affected.title: OpenSSL 4.0.0 to 4.0.3, or 4.1.0
affected.body: OpenSSL's CVE record lists only these versions; 3.x and older are not listed. Ubuntu disagrees in one place: it marks the Node.js package on Ubuntu 22.04, which bundles OpenSSL 1.1.1m, as vulnerable. Apps can also bundle their own OpenSSL. 1,7 openssl version

affected.title: Something encodes ~1.6 GB at once
affected.body: A program has to pass more than (INT_MAX / 4) * 3 bytes, about 1.6 GB, to EVP_EncodeBlock() in one call. Inside OpenSSL the known path is the proxy login of openssl s_client -proxy_pass , with the password read from an environment variable because a command line is too short to hold it. The fix changes only the base64 code and the HTTP proxy login code. 1,2

affected.title: An attacker controls that data
affected.body: The s_client proxy password is a setting chosen by whoever runs the command, so an attacker would already need to control your command or environment. Apps that call EVP_EncodeBlock() themselves on huge untrusted input would also be exposed. CISA's 9.8 assumes a remote attacker with no login; neither OpenSSL nor NVD has scored it. 2,1,3,5

actions.title: Update when 4.1.1 / 4.0.4 ship
actions.body: OpenSSL's CVE record names 4.1.1 and 4.0.4 as the first fixed versions, and OpenSSL has scheduled those releases for 1 Dec 2026. On 20 Nov the fix was still under review, on hold for discussion and not merged, so check the release notes. Debian and Ubuntu had not assessed their packages yet on 20 Nov. 1,4,2,9,7,8

actions.title: Only use proxy passwords you set
actions.body: If you script openssl s_client -proxy_pass , don't let other people supply the password or the environment variable it's read from. 2

actions.title: Cap input in your own code
actions.body: If your code calls EVP_EncodeBlock() on data from others, reject inputs over (INT_MAX / 4) * 3 bytes. That's the limit OpenSSL's fix enforces. 2
